doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Willcox on Joe Venuti and Stephane Grappelli
summary: Willcox praises Venuti as capable of any symphony and compares his playing to Grappelli's; they joke about Grappelli's nationality.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: You know Joe Venuti, now there’s a guy that I’ll bet any amount of money that he could step in any symphony, but there’s many a symphony guy that can play like Joe maybe in © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

the symphony but he can’t be far away, he wouldn’t even get in the front door. Oh, Joe Venuti. Can’t speak high enough of poor Joe Venuti. And there’s Stephane Grappelli, you know, Frenchman. You take those two guys, they both play just like their personality, in fact Stephane, he can play a lot of notes and he’s slipping and sliding, and he goes around on his tiptoes. He’s still alive though. But Joe Venuti played like an Italian.
But isn’t Grappelli Italian? It’s an Italian name.
Well maybe he is, but I’ll tell you, he acts like a Frenchman though. Boy we’ll have to check that out.
It doesn’t matter that much, they’re both great.
